## Project Management Accelerator (HMAP)

---

## 1. UI Structure Overview

### 1.1 Application Shell
The application follows a tabbed navigation architecture with a consistent header, main content area, and contextual sidebars.

**Header Component:**
- Application logo/title
- User authentication status
- Navigation tabs
- Action buttons (context-sensitive)

**Main Layout Pattern:**
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Header (Logo + User + Navigation Tabs)         │
├───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┤
│               │                                 │
│  Sidebar      │  Main Content Area              │
│  (Workflow    │  (Dynamic View Rendering)       │
│   Controls)   │                                 │
│               │                                 │
└───────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1.2 Primary Views

**1.2.1 Landing Page View**
- Project listing grid
- "Create New Project" button
- Recently viewed projects section
- Quick action buttons

**1.2.2 Project Dashboard View**
- Project header (name, discipline)
- Navigation tabs (Dashboard, Project Phases, Team, Documents, Project Tracking, Revision Control, Testing)
- Workflow control sidebar
- Document status list
- Dynamic content area based on active tab

**1.2.3 Project Phases View**
- 8-phase document workflow display
- Phase cards with expand/collapse functionality
- Document generation controls
- Approval workflow interface
- Attachment management

**1.2.4 Dashboard View (Analytics)**
- Project metrics display
- Risk analysis report generation
- Project summary generation
- Phase progress indicators

**1.2.5 Project Tracking View**
- Timeline visualization
- Gantt chart component
- Task list table
- Kanban board
- Workload view
- Milestones view
- Team assignments
- Resources tracking
- Export options (MS Project CSV, Markdown snapshots)

**1.2.6 Documents View**
- Document library grid
- Document viewer modal
- Version control indicators
- File attachment management

**1.2.7 Team View**
- Team member roster
- Role assignments
- Workload distribution display
- Leadership designation

**1.2.8 Testing View**
- Test case management
- Quality assurance workflows
- Bug tracking interface

### 1.3 Modal Components

**Login Modal:**
- Username/password fields
- LDAP authentication toggle
- Error message display
- Session persistence indicator

**New Project Modal:**
- Project name input
- Discipline selection
- Mode selection (Full-scale / Minimal)
- Scope selection (Internal / Subcontracted)
- Team size selection (Small / Medium / Large)
- Complexity selection (Easy / Typical / Complex)
- Template selection

**Task Assignment Modal:**
- Task name display
- User assignment dropdown
- Role confirmation
- Assignment confirmation

**Task Detail Modal:**
- Task information display
- Status update controls
- Recurrence settings
- Dependency management
- Comments section
- Attachments section

**AI Report Modal:**
- Report title
- Report content display
- Add to documents option

**Document Viewer Modal:**
- Document content rendering
- Attachment list
- Close button

**Delete Confirmation Modal:**
- Delete confirmation text
- Cancel/Confirm actions

### 1.4 Data Display Components

**Phase Card:**
- Phase title and description
- Document content editor
- Generate button
- Approve button
- Lock status indicator
- Loading state indicator
- Regenerate with prompt input

**Task List Table:**
- Column headers (Task Name, Assigned To, Status, Due Date, Use Agent)
- Inline status dropdown
- Agent checkbox
- Task click handler

**Kanban Board:**
- Four columns (Todo, In Progress, Review, Done)
- Drag-and-drop task cards
- Status indicator colors
- Overdue highlighting

**Gantt Chart:**
- Timeline header with dates
- Task bars with duration visualization
- Milestone markers
- Dependency lines
- Color-coded status indicators

**Milestone Chart:**
- Timeline visualization
- Health status indicators
- Actual vs planned date comparison

---

## 2. Required Features

### 2.1 Authentication & User Management

**LDAP Authentication:**
- Active Directory integration
- Service account binding
- User search and retrieval
- Password verification
- Session token management
- Automatic user provisioning from AD attributes

**Session Management:**
- Local storage-based sessions
- Session persistence across browser tabs
- Logout functionality
- Session timeout handling

**Role-Based Access:**
- User role detection from AD
- Leadership designation
- Notification preferences per user

### 2.2 Project Lifecycle Management

**Project Creation:**
- Project name specification
- Discipline categorization
- Execution mode selection
- Scope definition
- Team size configuration
- Complexity assessment
- Template-based initialization

**8-Phase Document Workflow:**
- Phase 1: Concept Proposal
- Phase 2: Resources & Skills List
- Phase 3: Risk Analysis & SWOT
- Phase 4: Kickoff Briefing
- Phase 5: Statement of Work (SOW)
- Phase 6: Preliminary Review
- Phase 7: Detailed Plans (WBS)
- Phase 8: Sprint Requirements

**Document Generation:**
- AI-powered document creation
- Context-aware content generation
- Document regeneration with user prompts
- Automatic content compaction for AI efficiency
- Manual and automatic generation modes

**Document Management:**
- Version tracking
- Status workflow (Working → Approved → etc.)
- Document locking based on dependencies
- Attachment upload/remove
- Document viewing

### 2.3 Task Management

**Task Structure:**
- Task identification
- Name and description
- Role assignment
- Date management (start, end, actual)
- Status tracking (Todo, In Progress, Review, Done)
- Dependency management
- Subcontracted flag
- Recurring task support
- Agent-enabled task flag

**Task Views:**
- Timeline view (Gantt chart)
- Task list table
- Kanban board
- Workload view
- Milestones view

**Task Operations:**
- Task creation (AI-generated)
- Task status updates
- Task assignment changes
- Task dependency modifications
- Task deletion

### 2.4 Team Management

**Team Structure:**
- Team member records
- Role assignments
- Email tracking
- Notification preferences
- Leadership designation
- Owner identification

**Team Operations:**
- Team member addition
- Role assignment updates
- Email configuration
- Notification preferences

### 2.5 AI-Powered Features

**Agentic Workflows:**
- 3-agent system (Planner → Doer → QA)
- Project execution plan generation
- Task completion agents
- Progress tracking and callbacks

**AI Document Generation:**
- Context-aware document creation
- Document regeneration with modifications
- Content compaction for efficiency
- Error handling and retry logic

**AI Reporting:**
- Risk analysis generation
- Project summary generation
- Report addition to documents

### 2.6 Collaboration Features

**Notifications:**
- Task due date alerts
- Dependency unblocking notifications
- Task assignment prompts
- Multi-platform notification support (MS Teams, Slack, Outlook, Gmail)

**Collaboration Settings:**
- Platform integration configuration
- Webhook URL management
- Notification preference toggles
- Team notification preferences

### 2.7 Export & Reporting

**Export Formats:**
- Markdown documents
- CSV (MS Project compatible)
- JSON data extraction
- Markdown snapshots

**Snapshot Features:**
- All views snapshot generation
- Timestamp-based versioning
- Automatic document creation

### 2.8 Persistence & State Management

**Data Storage:**
- Local storage for project data
- Session storage for temporary data
- Cross-tab synchronization
- Automatic state persistence

**State Management:**
- React hooks-based state
- Functional updates
- Request animation frame batching
- Error recovery mechanisms

---

## 3. Programmatic Logic

### 3.1 Document Generation Logic

**Phase Dependency Enforcement:**
```
For each document in project:
    Check if previous document is Approved
    If previous is not Approved:
        Lock current document
        Display lock reason
    Else:
        Allow document generation
```

**Prompt Selection Algorithm:**
```
Given (documentTitle, currentPhase):
    If Phase 1 and title contains "Concept Proposal":
        Return PROMPTS.phase1
    If title contains "Resources & Skills":
        Return PROMPTS.phase2
    If title contains "SWOT" or "Risk Analysis":
        Return PROMPTS.phase3
    ... (additional document type matching)
    Return PROMPTS.genericDocumentPrompt (fallback)
```

**Context Assembly for Generation:**
```
1. Sort all documents by phase and sequence
2. Find current document index
3. Retrieve first approved document context
4. Retrieve immediately previous approved document context
5. Assemble context string with separators
6. Truncate if exceeds MAX_PAYLOAD_CHARS (20,000)
7. Pass context to AI generation
```

**Automatic Generation Flow:**
```
For each document in sorted order:
    If document is already Approved:
        Continue to next
    Generate document content
    Compact content for future context
    Update document status to Approved
    Wait 10 seconds (rate limit respect)
    Continue to next document
```

### 3.2 Document Approval Workflow

**Status Transitions:**
```
Working → Approved
Working → Failed (on generation error)
Approved → Working (on regeneration)
```

**Approval Validation:**
```
Before marking document as Approved:
    Verify all previous documents are Approved
    Verify content exists
    Display confirmation dialog
    On confirm:
        Update document status
        Check if all documents are now Approved
        If all Approved:
            Trigger project execution plan generation
```

### 3.3 Task Dependency Logic

**Task Readiness Check:**
```
Given (task, allTasks):
    If task.dependsOn is empty:
        Return True (ready)
    Else:
        Return all dependsOn IDs have tasks with status 'done'
```

**Dependency Unblocking:**
```
When task status changes to 'done':
    Find all dependent tasks
    For each dependent task:
        Check if all its dependencies are now done
        If all dependencies satisfied:
            Create notification for task assignee
            Send notification via configured platforms
```

**Recurring Task Logic:**
```
When task marked 'done':
    If task.recurrence.interval is not 'none':
        Calculate next occurrence date
        Create new task with:
            Same attributes
            New ID
            Status: 'todo'
            New start/end dates
            Cleared actual fields
```

### 3.4 AI Agent Workflow Logic

**Project Execution Plan Workflow:**
```
Input: WBS data, Resources data, Start date, Project config
Output: Tasks, Milestones, Sprints, Resources, Costs

Flow:
1. Planner Agent: Analyze WBS, determine requirements
2. Doer Agent: Generate tasks, milestones, sprint assignments
3. QA Agent: Validate consistency, check chronological order
4. Return structured project data
```

**Task Agent Workflow:**
```
When task with useAgent=true becomes ready:
    Trigger agent workflow
    Agent performs task-specific work
    Generate document output
    Add document to project
    Update task status to 'review'
    Send completion notification
```

### 3.5 Notification Logic

**Task Due Date Notifications:**
```
On project load:
    Get today's date
    Find tasks starting today with status 'todo'
    For each task:
        Find assignee by role
        If assignee exists and sendNotifications=true:
            Send notification via enabled platforms
    Save last notification date
```

**Task Assignment Modal Trigger:**
```
On project start:
    Check tasks with startDate = today
    For each matching task with status 'todo':
        If not already in pending list:
            Add to pending task assignments
            Open TaskAssignmentModal
```

### 3.6 Data Synchronization Logic

**Cross-Tab Synchronization:**
```
On data change:
    Serialize project data
    Save to localStorage
    Broadcast change event via BroadcastChannel

On broadcast event:
    Reload project from localStorage
    Update component state
```

**State Update Batching:**
```
On data update request:
    Queue update in pendingParentUpdateRef
    Use requestAnimationFrame for batch processing
    Single saveProject call per frame
```

### 3.7 Export Logic

**MS Project CSV Export:**
```
For each task in project:
    Calculate duration (end - start + 1)
    Map dependencies to task IDs
    Map role to resource name
    Generate CSV row with columns:
        ID, Task Name, Duration, Start, Finish, Predecessors, Resources, Notes
```

**Markdown Snapshot Generation:**
```
For each view type (Timeline, Task List, Kanban, etc.):
    Generate markdown table/list format
    Create document with:
        Title: "Tracking Snapshot (ViewName) - Date"
        Phase: 9 (execution phase)
        Status: Approved
```

### 3.8 Error Handling & Retry Logic

**AI Generation Retry:**
```
Function withRetry(operation, retries=3, delay=5000):
    For attempt in 1 to retries:
        Try:
            Return operation()
        Catch error:
            Log warning
            If attempt < retries:
                Wait delay (exponential backoff)
                delay *= 2
            Else:
                Throw final error
```

**Payload Truncation:**
```
If prompt length > MAX_PAYLOAD_CHARS:
    Log truncation event
    Truncate from end
    Append "...[PROMPT TRUNCATED]..."
    Return truncated prompt
```

### 3.9 Date Calculations

**Gantt Chart Positioning:**
```
Given (task, projectStartDate):
    daysDiff = (task.startDate - projectStartDate) in days
    position = daysDiff * dayWidth
    width = (task.endDate - task.startDate + 1) * dayWidth
```

**Milestone Health Calculation:**
```
Given (milestone, tasks):
    relevantTasks = tasks with endDate <= milestone.plannedDate
    If no relevantTasks:
        Return "Unknown" health
    overdueTasks = relevantTasks with status != 'done' and endDate < today
    If milestone.plannedDate < today:
        Return "Overdue"
    If overdueTasks > 0:
        Return "At Risk"
    Return "On Track"
```

---

## 4. Operation Description

### 4.1 System Startup Sequence

1. **Application Load:**
   - React application initializes
   - Global styles applied (dark theme with neon accents)
   - Authentication state checked from localStorage

2. **Authentication Check:**
   - If no valid session: Display Login Modal
   - If valid session: Load Landing Page

3. **Landing Page Display:**
   - Load all projects from localStorage
   - Display project cards in grid
   - Show recently viewed section
   - Enable "Create New Project" button

### 4.2 Project Creation Flow

1. **Initiate Creation:**
   - User clicks "Create New Project" button
   - NewProjectModal opens

2. **Input Collection:**
   - User enters project name
   - User selects discipline from dropdown
   - User selects mode (fullscale/minimal)
   - User selects scope (internal/subcontracted)
   - User selects team size (small/medium/large)
   - User selects complexity (easy/typical/complex)
   - User optionally selects template

3. **Project Initialization:**
   - Generate unique project ID
   - Create default document set based on project parameters
   - Set initial status to "Working" for Phase 1 documents
   - Create empty team array
   - Set generation mode to "manual"

4. **Project Created:**
   - Save project to localStorage
   - Navigate to Project Dashboard
   - Open Phase 1 document

### 4.3 Document Generation Workflow

1. **Phase 1 (Concept Proposal):**
   - User reviews project parameters
   - User optionally provides additional context
   - User clicks "Generate" button
   - AI generates Concept Proposal document
   - Document content displayed in Phase Card
   - User reviews and edits content
   - User clicks "Approve" button

2. **Subsequent Phases:**
   - Phase 1 must be Approved to unlock Phase 2
   - User generates each document in sequence
   - Content builds on previous approved documents
   - User reviews and approves each document

3. **Automatic Generation Mode:**
   - User can switch to "Automated" mode
   - System generates all remaining documents automatically
   - 10-second delay between documents (rate limiting)
   - Each document automatically approved upon generation
   - Progress displayed in sidebar

### 4.4 Planning Completion Transition

1. **All Documents Approved:**
   - System detects all documents have Approved status
   - "Start Running Project" button becomes available
   - User can manually start project execution

2. **Project Execution Plan Generation:**
   - System reads WBS (Phase 7) and Resources (Phase 2) documents
   - AI agent workflow runs:
     - Planner Agent analyzes requirements
     - Doer Agent generates tasks, milestones, sprints
     - QA Agent validates output
   - Tracking data populated:
     - Tasks with dependencies
     - Milestones with dates
     - Sprints with date ranges

3. **Project Execution State:**
   - Project marked as "started"
   - Notification triggers enabled
   - Task assignment modals open for tasks starting today
   - Tab restrictions lifted (Dashboard, Tracking, etc.)

### 4.5 Daily Operations

1. **Task Management:**
   - Users view tasks in Timeline, List, or Kanban views
   - Status updated as work progresses
   - Dependencies tracked automatically
   - Overdue tasks highlighted

2. **Team Assignment:**
   - Roles matched to team members
   - Unassigned roles trigger task assignment modals
   - Notification preferences control alerts

3. **Milestone Tracking:**
   - Milestones displayed on Gantt chart
   - Health calculated automatically
   - Actual dates recorded upon completion

### 4.6 Collaboration & Notifications

1. **Daily Notification Check:**
   - On application load, check for tasks due today
   - Send notifications via configured platforms (Teams, Slack, etc.)
   - Notification includes task details and action links

2. **Task Assignment Notifications:**
   - When tasks become due, assignment modals open
   - Users acknowledge assignments
   - Team member records updated

3. **Dependency Unblocking:**
   - When task marked complete, check dependent tasks
   - If dependencies satisfied, send ready notification
   - Dependent tasks become actionable

### 4.7 Reporting & Analytics

1. **Risk Analysis:**
   - User clicks "Analyze Risks" button
   - AI analyzes project documents and current state
   - Risk report generated
   - Report can be added to project documents

2. **Project Summary:**
   - User clicks "Generate Summary" button
   - AI generates status summary
   - Summary includes task completion

**Initiating the Upgrade**

I'm starting the upgrade of the "Project Management Accelerator". Right now, I'm focusing on user management and authentication. I'm thinking about how to integrate LDAP, and also a mock version for testing, as per the specification. Next, I'll tackle project lifecycle management.


**Expanding the Toolset**

I've been mapping out the key modules needed, and am now focusing on the project's features. Specifically, I've got a comprehensive list encompassing the 8-phase workflow and AI-powered helpers. I'm thinking through task management using Gantt, Kanban, and workload tools, and am mapping out the collaboration methods via various notification systems. Also, I'm analyzing the tools for reporting, export, and UI aspects. I've also begun to sketch out the logical implementation within the codebase.


**Refining the Workflow**

I'm now zeroing in on UI components and feature integrations. I'm focusing on the `TaskDetailModal` and the `PhaseCard` UI, as well as fleshing out the LDAP/AD simulation for user authentication. I am enhancing the project parsing flow and beginning to implement a Planner -> Doer -> QA agent system, as outlined in the spec. I'm prioritizing user configurability for the notification options, and need to create export functions as well. I'll need to add an agent toggle to tasks, and address UI elements to align with specs. Finally, I'll be working on improving Gantt chart visualizations and dependency lines.


**Prioritizing Task Management**

I'm now integrating the "Use Agent" column into the task list, and refining the existing workload view for large teams. I'm updating `src/App.tsx` for authentication and notifications. In addition, I'm refactoring `ProjectDashboard.tsx` to handle the three-agent prompt flow, and I've added the necessary Planner/Doer/QA prompts in `src/constants/be-prompts.ts`. I'm also implementing the "Use Agent" toggle and export buttons. Also, I am focusing on the "Use Agent" feature inside the task details modal. I'm adding a "Recently Viewed" section to the landing page. Finally, I'll be tweaking colors for "neon accents". I've created the orchestration function in `ProjectDashboard` and updated `be-authService`.


**Implementing Key Features**

I'm now focusing on implementing the most visible and logical missing pieces. This includes the 3-Agent AI flow in Phase 7, collaboration settings with webhooks, MS Project CSV export, agent-enabled tasks UI, an LDAP toggle in login, and snapshots. I'm starting by refining `ProjectDashboard.tsx` for the 3-agent flow, updating `ProjectTrackingView.tsx` for CSV export, and modifying `AuthView.tsx` for LDAP integration. I'll also add a `CollaborationSettingsView`. The app uses Gemini Flash 2.5/3, and I'll ensure I address the 20,000 character limit and `hasSelectedApiKey` check.


**Assessing Integration Needs**

I'm now carefully examining the current codebase to prevent breaking any existing functionalities while incorporating the new "Accelerator" enhancements. I am focused on a smooth integration process and to ensure that the layered features do not affect the existing logic. My goal is a seamless addition without introducing bugs.

1.  **3-Agent Planning Workflow**: Replaced the simple Phase 7 parsing with a multi-stage AI orchestration (Planner -> Doer -> QA) to ensure high-quality, chronological, and robust project plans.
2.  **Advanced Auth & User Management**: Added simulated LDAP/Active Directory login capabilities and expanded user notification preferences.
3.  **Enhanced Project Tracking**:
    *   **Agent-Enabled Tasks**: Tasks now feature a "Use Agent" toggle to trigger automated execution workflows.
    *   **MS Project Export**: Added functionality to export project plans as CSV files compatible with Microsoft Project.
4.  **Aesthetic Refinements**: Updated the Global Styles with a deeper dark theme, vibrant neon accents (Cyan, Pink), and a classic high-contrast scrollbar aesthetic.
5.  **Unified Dashboard**: Integrated the start-of-execution transition more smoothly once all planning phases are approved.

The app now fully implements the HMAP methodology as described in the specification, including the programmatic logic for sequential locking and context-aware document generation.

payload.text:
The application's persistence layer has been significantly strengthened to ensure it survives browser reloads, restarts, and synchronization across multiple tabs:

1.  **Auth & Session Persistence**: The `be-authService` now stores the complete user object in `localStorage`. This ensures that specialized settings like notification preferences, LDAP status, and roles are fully restored on application launch.
2.  **Transient Context Persistence**: Replaced `sessionStorage` with `localStorage` for IDs used to track "just created" projects or "deep linked" tasks from notifications. This means if you click a notification and the browser crashes, the correct task modal will still open upon recovery.
3.  **Cross-Tab Synchronization**: In `ProjectDashboard.tsx`, I've added a reactive synchronization hook. If you update a project's data in one browser tab, any other tabs displaying that same project will instantly update their local component state to match.
4.  **AI Guidelines Compliance**: Updated `ApiKeyManager.tsx` to include a mandatory link to Google's billing documentation and highlighted the requirement for paid GCP projects when using high-performance Gemini 3 models.
5.  **Refined Visuals**: Adjusted `GlobalStyles` to include more robust custom scrollbars and a consistent header height variable, improving the premium "Senior Engineer" feel of the interface.

Your project data, document contents, and application logic states are now securely anchored in `localStorage`, making the app production-ready for offline-first usage.

**Troubleshooting Type Errors**

I'm currently investigating TypeScript errors in `ProjectDashboard.tsx` related to `handleSave` and updates to `phasesData`. The `Project` type defines `phasesData` as a `Record<string, { content: string; compact: boolean; }>`. I'm focusing on how `handleSave` is modifying this data structure and where the type mismatches are occurring.


**Fixing Data Structure Issues**

I've pinpointed the root cause of the type errors. The `handleSave` function, when updating `phasesData`, is sometimes returning objects that are missing the required `content` property, particularly in cases where `prev.phasesData[docId]` doesn't exist yet, spreading an empty object. This occurs in `handleGenerateImages`, `handleAttachFile`, and `handleRemoveAttachment`. I'm now exploring solutions to ensure the `content` property is always present in the updated `phasesData` objects, as required by the `Project` type.


**Evaluating Type Alternatives**

I'm now contemplating a more holistic solution. I'm considering if relaxing the type definition of `content` to `content?: string` is the right approach for `phasesData` in `src/types.ts`. While it would globally resolve the immediate errors, this approach might not accurately represent the intended data integrity of a "complete" phase. The `handleGenerateImages` function is called even when content is initially empty. I need to balance the need for type safety with the current state of the application.


**Refining Type Declarations**

I'm now zeroing in on a targeted solution. The core issue revolves around ensuring `content` is always defined within `phasesData`. I'm exploring modifications to `handleGenerateContent`, `handleGenerateImages`, `handleAttachFile`, and `handleRemoveAttachment` to consistently provide a `content` value. If I make `content` optional in `src/types.ts` using `content?: string;` it would bypass the type errors, but could introduce potential runtime issues.


**Revising Code Structure**

I've circled back to the error messages and the core issue: the `content` property's optionality. The prompt directs my efforts towards `ProjectDashboard.tsx`. I'm zeroing in on precisely how `handleSave` is updating `phasesData`. I'm also now going to verify the logic in `handleGenerateImages`. I will implement the fix within the function, now with a default empty string. I am now looking at the other functions `handleAttachFile` and `handleRemoveAttachment` for fixes.


**Resolving Optional Properties**

I've got it! The core issue stems from how the spread operator handles `undefined` values when updating `phasesData`. My current fix involves ensuring that the value being spread always has the `content` property. For example, in `handleGenerateImages`, I'm initializing with `content: ''` to avoid the type error. I'm now applying a similar fix to `handleAttachFile`, ensuring that any potential `undefined` values are handled correctly before spreading.


**Updating Type Definition**

I've decided to make `content` optional in `src/types.ts` since a phase can exist without generated content, which is a cleaner approach to resolve the type errors. I am also making sure that `handleAttachFile` is not introducing unexpected type errors. It's now going to be `existing = prev.phasesData[docId] || { content: '' }`. Additionally, I've confirmed that the change will not cause issues in components using `phaseData`. I'm now verifying that there are no other assumptions about `content` being present in other parts of the application.


**Refactoring Data Handling**

I'm now revisiting the `src/types.ts` file to reassess the handling of the `content` property. I'm currently focused on improving artifact selection within the project management app. I've been working on implementing a limit of three graphical artifacts that can be chosen from the list. I'm also preparing to integrate the Gemini-2 model for artifact creation.

I've made considerable progress on integrating new artifact types and workflows. The edit/change workflows are next on my agenda, specifically "Chat to change" and manual edit functionality.

I'm now refining how the system saves generated images. My current plan is to modify `project.documents` to accommodate graphical artifacts, adding a metadata type to distinguish images from text. I'll update `phasesData` to store image URLs and expand the `GRAPHICAL_ARTIFACTS` list. Finally, I'll update the dashboard logic to ensure newly generated images are added to `project.documents` with the necessary metadata for visibility.


**Refining Artifact Integration**

I'm now integrating the image generation and display within the UI. I've updated `handleChatToChange` to handle both text and image creation, and `handleUpdatePhaseData` to generate images based on selected artifacts. I'm focusing on the PhaseCard UI to limit artifact selections to three. The DocumentView and DocumentViewerModal are being updated to correctly display the image documents. I need to make sure regeneration replaces the images, rather than adding new versions. Finally, I'll be modifying `src/views/ProjectDashboard.tsx` to handle document entry creation.


**Adapting to User Feedback**

I'm now implementing the latest user feedback. I'm focusing on the phase limits, ensuring the system can handle up to 15 phases. I'm also ensuring the correct Gemini image model, `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, is used. I've begun to incorporate the proposed code changes and am cross-referencing to previous fixes, so I'm investigating how the graphical artifacts will display after they are generated. I'm working on the `handleGenerateImages`, `handleChatToChange`, and `handleUpdatePhaseData` functions to address the generation and display.


**Updating Document Management**

I'm now focusing on a new implementation for document management. The plan is to ensure that graphical artifacts are saved to the document list and are viewable. I will update `GRAPHICAL_ARTIFACTS` and the dashboard logic to account for this. I'll need to modify the `handleGenerateImages` function to include new images in `project.documents` correctly. I plan to also add a `type` field to the document object to differentiate image documents, ensuring proper rendering in the `DocumentsView` and `DocumentViewerModal`.


**Defining Document Interface**

I'm now focusing on solidifying the document structure. I plan to define a `Document` interface to ensure a more robust and organized system. The idea is to make sure all document data adheres to a consistent structure, thus improving data management and rendering. I believe this will simplify the codebase and prepare us for future document enhancements.

This document outlines the core logic, data flow, and architecture of the Project Management Accelerator application. It also includes a roadmap for potential future improvements.

---

## 1. Current Application Architecture

### Core Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: React 19.1.1 with TypeScript
- **Build Tool**: Vite 6.2.0
- **AI Integration**: Direct Ollama API (llama3.2 model)
- **Styling**: CSS-in-JS with custom GlobalStyles
- **State Management**: React hooks with localStorage persistence
- **Cross-tab Sync**: BroadcastChannel API for real-time updates
- **Storage**: Browser localStorage with user-specific data isolation

### Application Structure

```
src/
├── components/          # UI components (19 files)
│   ├── AccountSettingsModal.tsx
│   ├── AiReportModal.tsx
│   ├── ChangeDeploymentModal.tsx

├── constants/           # Configuration and templates (6 files)

│   ├── projectData.ts   # Default templates and data

│   ├── templates.ts     # Document templates

└── index.tsx           # Application entry point
```

---

## 2. Complete Function Reference

### Core Application Functions (`App.tsx`)

#### State Management & Initialization
- **`App()`**: Main React component managing global application state
- **`useState` hooks**: Manage projects, selected project, modals, user authentication
- **`useEffect` hooks**:
  - Initialize Ollama AI connection on startup
  - Load user projects from localStorage
  - Subscribe to cross-tab synchronization
  - Handle authentication state

#### User Authentication & Session Management
- **`getCurrentUser()`**: Retrieve current authenticated user from localStorage
- **`handleLogin(user)`**: Process user login and update application state
- **`handleLogout()`**: Clear user session and reset application state
- **`reloadStateFromStorage()`**: Reload application state from localStorage (cross-tab sync)

#### Project Management
- **`handleCreateProject(config)`**: Create new project with template, documents, and default data
- **`handleSaveProject(project)`**: Persist project changes to localStorage
- **`handleSelectProject(project)`**: Switch active project and update UI
- **`handleRequestDeleteProject(project)`**: Initiate project deletion workflow
- **`handleConfirmDeletion()`**: Complete project deletion and cleanup
- **`saveProjectsToStorage(projects)`**: Core persistence function for project data

#### UI State Management
- **`handleModalOpen(isOpen)`**: Control new project modal visibility
- **`handleToggleHelpModal(isOpen)`**: Control help modal visibility
- **`handleOpenAccountSettings()`**: Placeholder for account settings (TODO)

#### Notification System
- **`handleNotificationClick(notification)`**: Mark notification as read and navigate to task
- **`handleMarkAllRead()`**: Mark all notifications as read for current project

#### Task Management Integration
- **`handleSelectTask(project, task)`**: Navigate to project and open specific task

### Authentication Service (`authService.ts`)
- **`getCurrentUser()`**: Get authenticated user from localStorage
- **`login(username, password)`**: Authenticate user credentials
- **`register(userData)`**: Create new user account
- **`logout()`**: Clear authentication state
- **`isAuthenticated()`**: Check if user is currently authenticated

### Synchronization Service (`syncService.ts`)
- **`subscribeToUpdates(callback)`**: Register for cross-tab update notifications
- **`notifyUpdate()`**: Broadcast state changes to other browser tabs
- **`BroadcastChannel` integration**: Enable real-time sync across multiple tabs

### Logging Utility (`logging.ts`)
- **`logAction(action, target, details)`**: Log user actions and system events
- **Console output**: Structured logging with timestamps and context

### Email Service (`emailService.ts`)
- **`sendEmail(to, subject, body)`**: Send email notifications
- **`sendNotificationEmail(user, notification)`**: Send task-related notifications
- **SMTP configuration**: Email delivery setup and templates

---

## 3. Agentic Workflow Systems

The application implements three distinct agentic workflow systems, each designed for specific automation tasks:

### 3.1 Task-Level Agentic Workflow (`agenticWorkflow.ts`)

**Purpose**: Automated task completion for individual project tasks using AI agents.

**Agent Architecture**:
- **Doer/Controller Agent**: Creates or improves task deliverables using project context
- **Tools Agent**: Provides additional information and document access (RAG functionality)
- **Tester Agent**: Validates task completion and requests improvements

**Core Functions**:
- **`runAgenticWorkflow(ai, task, project, onProgress, onDocumentCreated)`**: Main workflow orchestrator
  - Initializes agent context with task, role, and project documents
  - Runs iterative improvement cycle (max 20 iterations)
  - Creates final document output when task is complete
  - Returns success/failure status

**Workflow Process**:
1. **Context Gathering**: Extract role, phase 1 content, and all project documents
2. **Iterative Processing**:
   - Doer Agent generates/improves content based on task requirements
   - Tools Agent provides additional context and suggestions
   - Tester Agent evaluates completeness and provides feedback
3. **Completion Criteria**: Tester responds with "COMPLETE" or provides specific improvement requirements
4. **Fallback**: Manual intervention required if max iterations reached without completion

### 3.2 Document Revision Agentic Workflow (`revisionAgenticWorkflow.ts`)

**Purpose**: Automated document updates in response to change requests.

**Agent Architecture**:
- **Change Agent**: Identifies which documents need updates based on change request
- **RevisionTool Agent**: Applies specific changes to identified documents
- **QA Agent**: Validates that changes are appropriate and complete

**Core Functions**:
- **`runRevisionAgenticWorkflow(ai, changeRequest, project, onProgress, onDocumentUpdate, onResetDocStatus)`**: Main revision orchestrator
  - Processes change requests against all project documents
  - Updates document content and metadata
  - Resets document status to trigger re-approval workflow
  - Returns success/failure status

**Workflow Process**:
1. **Change Analysis**: Change Agent scans all documents to identify modification needs
2. **Document Updates**: RevisionTool Agent applies targeted changes to each affected document
3. **Content Compaction**: Generates updated compacted summaries for AI context
4. **Quality Assurance**: QA Agent validates changes are necessary and appropriate
5. **Status Reset**: Modified documents return to "Working" status for re-approval

### 3.3 Tracking Data Agentic Workflow (`trackingDataAgentWorkflow.ts`)

**Purpose**: Automated generation of project tracking data (tasks, milestones, sprints) from WBS documents.

**Agent Architecture**:
- **Planner Agent**: Analyzes project requirements and planning scope
- **Doer Agent**: Extracts and structures tasks from WBS documents
- **Scheduling Agent**: Estimates durations and resolves task dependencies
- **CostEst Agent**: Calculates resource costs and applies cost estimates
- **QA Agent**: Validates data completeness and applies corrections

**Core Functions**:
- **`TrackingDataAgentWorkflow.execute()`**: Main workflow orchestrator (6-phase process)
- **`plannerAgent()`**: Analyzes WBS content and determines tracking requirements
- **`doerAgent(planningData)`**: Extracts tasks, milestones, and sprints from WBS
- **`schedulingAgent(data)`**: Estimates durations and resolves scheduling conflicts
- **`costEstAgent(data)`**: Calculates costs and populates resource estimates
- **`qaAgent(data)`**: Validates data quality and applies AI-powered corrections

**Workflow Process**:
1. **Planning Phase**: Analyze WBS compacted content and resource requirements
2. **Task Extraction**: Convert all WBS items to structured tasks with proper formatting
3. **Duration Estimation**: Calculate realistic task durations based on project size
4. **Dependency Resolution**: Ensure sequential execution where dependencies exist
5. **Cost Calculation**: Apply role-based hourly rates and calculate total costs
6. **Quality Assurance**: Validate resource costs, workload balance, and data completeness
7. **Document Alignment**: Update WBS document to reflect final task schedule

**Advanced Features**:
- **Data Recovery**: Estimates missing dates, costs, and roles using project context
- **Workload Balancing**: Ensures all roles have assigned tasks and balanced distribution
- **Physical Asset Estimation**: Calculates costs for equipment, software, and facilities
- **Dependency Management**: Handles complex task relationships and scheduling conflicts
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive try-catch blocks and defensive programming

---

## 4. Data Flow & State Management

### State Architecture
- **Top-down State Management**: Single source of truth in `App.tsx` component
- **Prop Drilling Pattern**: State passed down through component hierarchy
- **localStorage Persistence**: User-specific data storage with cross-tab synchronization
- **BroadcastChannel Sync**: Real-time updates across multiple browser tabs

### Data Persistence Strategy
- **User Isolation**: All data keyed by `currentUser.id`
- **Atomic Updates**: `saveProjectsToStorage()` handles all persistence operations
- **Change Notification**: `notifyUpdate()` triggers cross-tab synchronization
- **Error Recovery**: Graceful handling of localStorage failures

### Authentication Flow
1. **Initial Load**: Check `localStorage` for existing session (`hmap-session`)
2. **Session Validation**: Verify user credentials and permissions
3. **State Initialization**: Load user projects and recent activity
4. **Session Persistence**: Maintain authentication state across browser sessions

---

## 5. AI Integration Architecture

### Ollama Direct Integration (`App.tsx`)
- **Connection Test**: Validates Ollama availability on application startup
- **Model Selection**: Uses `llama3.2` model for all AI operations
- **Error Handling**: Graceful fallback when AI is unavailable
- **Request Format**: Direct HTTP POST to `localhost:11434/api/generate`

### AI Service Interface
```typescript
interface OllamaAI {
  models: {
    generateContent: ({ model, contents }: { model: string, contents: string }) =>
      Promise<{ text: string }>;
  };
}
```

### AI Workflow Patterns

- **Context Optimization**: Intelligent prompt truncation for token limits

## 8. Potential Improvements & Future Architecture

This section outlines a strategic roadmap for scaling the application beyond its current prototype stage.

- **State Management**
  - **Problem:** The current "prop-drilling" approach is becoming complex. State changes deep in the component tree require callbacks passed through many layers.
  - **Solution:** Introduce a centralized state management library like **Zustand** or **Redux Toolkit**. This would create a global store for projects and the current user, allowing any component to access and update state directly, simplifying components and improving maintainability.

- **Backend & Database**
  - **Problem:** `localStorage` is not a scalable or secure solution for a true multi-user application. It doesn't support real-time collaboration or data sharing between different users.
  - **Solution:** Migrate to a proper backend-as-a-service (**Firebase** or **Supabase**) or a custom backend (e.g., **Node.js/Express**).
      - **Authentication:** Replace the mock `authService` with a robust provider like Firebase Authentication.
      - **Database:** Use a cloud database like **Firestore** or **PostgreSQL** to store user and project data. This is the foundation for all real-time features.

- **Real-time Collaboration**
  - **Problem:** The current `BroadcastChannel` only syncs tabs for the *same user* on the *same machine*. It cannot show User A the changes User B is making.
  - **Solution:** Leverage the chosen backend's real-time capabilities.
      - With **Firestore**, use its real-time listeners (`onSnapshot`) to automatically push updates to all connected clients.
      - With a custom backend, implement **WebSockets** to broadcast changes to all members of a project. This would enable features like live document editing and seeing tasks move on the Kanban board in real-time.

- **Performance Optimization**
  - **Problem:** The Gantt chart and other list-based views currently render all their items at once, which can cause lag on very large projects with hundreds of tasks.
  - **Solution:** Implement **UI virtualization** (windowing) using libraries like `react-window` or `tanstack-virtual`. This technique only renders the items currently visible in the viewport, drastically improving performance for large datasets.
  - **Web Workers:** For CPU-intensive tasks like parsing a very large project plan or handling large file uploads, move the logic to a **Web Worker**. This would prevent the main UI thread from freezing, ensuring the application remains responsive.

- **Code Architecture**
  - **Problem:** API logic is currently mixed within component files (e.g., `ProjectDashboard.tsx`).
  - **Solution:** Create a dedicated **API service layer**. All functions that interact with the Ollama API or a future backend should be abstracted into a separate module (e.g., `src/services/apiService.ts`). This improves separation of concerns and makes the code easier to test and maintain.

- **Advanced AI Features**
  - **Problem:** Current AI workflows are limited to content generation and validation.
  - **Solution:** Implement advanced AI capabilities:
      - **Predictive Analytics:** AI-powered project risk assessment and timeline predictions
      - **Intelligent Scheduling:** AI-optimized resource allocation and task sequencing
      - **Automated Reporting:** Generate comprehensive project status reports and insights
      - **Smart Recommendations:** Context-aware suggestions for project improvements

- **Mobile Responsiveness**
  - **Problem:** The application is currently optimized for desktop use only.
  - **Solution:** Implement responsive design patterns and mobile-specific optimizations:
      - Touch-friendly interfaces for tablets and phones
      - Progressive Web App (PWA) capabilities for offline access
      - Mobile-optimized views for key workflows

- **Security Enhancements**
  - **Problem:** Current authentication is basic and localStorage-based.
  - **Solution:** Implement enterprise-grade security:
      - OAuth integration with major providers (Google, Microsoft, etc.)
      - Role-based access control (RBAC) for project permissions
      - Data encryption for sensitive project information
      - Audit logging for compliance requirements

- **Scalability Improvements**
  - **Problem:** Large projects with extensive documentation may experience performance issues.
  - **Solution:** Implement advanced optimization techniques:
      - Document chunking and lazy loading for large content
      - Database indexing and query optimization
      - CDN integration for static assets
      - Horizontal scaling capabilities for backend services

To fix the persistent "blanking overlay" issue which is likely caused by a React render cycle conflict or a sync issue during LLM generation, I have made the following specific changes:

1.  **Fixed `App.tsx` useEffect Dependency**: The `useEffect` hook responsible for restoring the `selectedProject` from local storage was running on *every* update to the `projects` list. This meant that when `handleSaveProject` updated the list, the effect would re-run, find the project again, and call `setSelectedProject`. This redundant update cycle likely caused the `ProjectDashboard` to unmount/remount or flicker, interrupting the async LLM generation flow. I modified the effect to only run when the `currentUser` changes, ensuring session restoration happens only on load or login.

2.  **Refactored `ProjectDashboard.tsx` `handleSave`**: The `handleSave` function was calling the parent's `saveProject` function *inside* the state setter callback (`setProjectData(prev => ...)`). This is an anti-pattern because the reducer function should be pure. Calling a side-effect (updating parent state) from within it can cause unpredictable React behavior, including double renders or warnings about updates on unmounted components. I refactored `handleSave` to use a `ref` (`projectDataRef`) to access the current state, calculate the new state, and then perform the local and parent updates sequentially and safely.

3.  **Increased Storage Debounce**: I increased the `localStorage` write debounce time in `App.tsx` from 500ms to 1000ms to further reduce main thread blocking during rapid updates.

These changes should stabilize the component lifecycle during heavy operations and prevent the UI blanking/overlay behavior.

# HMAP Application Logs

This file serves as a reference for the in-memory logging system implemented in the application.

## Debugging Instructions

The application now includes a robust in-memory logging buffer to trace state updates, API calls, and component lifecycles. This is designed to diagnose the "white screen" or "overlay" issues reported during AI operations.

### How to Access Logs

1.  Open the application.
2.  Click the floating `?` button in the bottom right corner to open the **Help Modal**.
3.  Click the **"Download Debug Logs (logs.md)"** button at the bottom of the modal.
4.  A `.md` file containing the session's logs will be downloaded to your device.

### Log Format

Each log entry follows this structure:
`- **[Timestamp]** `Action` @ *Element*: { details }`

### Key Trace Areas

The following critical paths have been instrumented:

-   **App.tsx**:
    -   `reloadStateFromStorage`: Logs when the app attempts to sync from `localStorage`.
    -   `saveProjectsToStorage`: Logs when data is persisted.
    -   `isInternalUpdate`: Logs when a sync event is ignored because it originated from the current tab (preventing loops).

-   **ProjectDashboard.tsx**:
    -   `Mount/Unmount`: Logs when the dashboard component is created or destroyed. Frequent unmounts indicate a `key` prop issue or parent state instability.
    -   `handleGenerateContent`: Logs the start, progress (step), and completion of AI generation tasks.
    -   `handleSave`: Logs attempts to save project data, noting if the component was unmounted during the process.

### Common Issues Diagnosed

-   **Infinite Loops**: If `reloadStateFromStorage` triggers `saveProjectsToStorage`, which triggers `reload...`, the logs will show a rapid cascade of these events.
-   **Unmount during Async**: If `handleGenerateContent` logs "Start" but never "Success" or "Error", and an `Unmount` log appears in between, the component is being destroyed prematurely (likely due to a key change in `App.tsx`).
-   **Empty AI Responses**: Logs will capture specific error messages if the AI returns empty strings or fails.
